title: The role of long-term memory, flexible templates and learning in attentional guidance
abstract: Nature Reviews Psychology, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44159-026-00626-2 Theories of visual search suggest that humans hold a veridical representation of the desired target in working memory to guide attention. In this Review, Carlisle and Woodman synthesize evidence that attentional guidance is flexible, adaptive on the basis of experience, and driven by multiple coordinated mechanisms.
